mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets the model invent an Operation whose (caller.role, kind) pair is outside the permission matrix; the injection forces such a violating operation to exist, so LeastPrivilege must produce a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = PostDecision }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the canonicality fact lets two distinct ApplicationEvent atoms record the same status change for the same application; the injection forces that duplication, which is the structural shape of an append-only violation in a snapshot model.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.application = e2.application and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows two Decision atoms for the same application; the injection demands exactly that, so the concurrency-safety assertion must find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoDecisions { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = d2.application }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets a Customer-roled caller's Operation target an application owned by someone else; the injection forces that scenario, which is exactly the FR-013 leak.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation, u: User | op.caller.role = Customer and some op.target and op.target.customer = u and u != op.caller and u.role = Customer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the partial-unique-index fact lets a single customer hold two Pending Review applications simultaneously; the injection forces that state to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoPendingPerCustomer { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets an application exist without its corresponding submitted audit event; the injection forces that gap, so AuditCompleteness must counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingSubmittedEvent { some a: LoanApplication | no e: ApplicationEvent | e.application = a and e.eventType = SubmittedEvent }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets a decision event's actor differ from the actual decider; the injection forces a decision event with an actor that no Decision row attests, which is the precise shape of misattribution.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionMismatch { some e: ApplicationEvent | (e.eventType = ApprovedEvent or e.eventType = RejectedEvent) and (no d: Decision | d.application = e.application and d.decidedBy = e.actor) }
